title: The Measurement Problem: What Happens When We Look?
question: Why does a quantum system behave as a spread of possibilities until it's observed, and what actually counts as an 'observation'?
summary: Quantum mechanics predicts a superposition of outcomes right up until measurement, at which point one outcome becomes real. A century after the theory's founding, physicists still cannot agree on what a measurement physically is, or why it seems to change the rules.
